## Paid Campaign Strategies: Social Commerce and Traditional Arbitrage


### Navigating Policy Compliance: Avoiding Direct Link Bans on Meta and Google


Direct links from ads to affiliate destinations can create policy and quality problems. Platforms need to know who controls the destination, what users receive, and whether the ad matches the post-click experience. Google Ads Bridge Page policy addresses pages made mainly to send users elsewhere without meaningful original value. Meta’s advertising terms require truthful representations, functional destinations, and legal compliance.


Use a landing page that explains the offer, identifies the commercial relationship, provides useful context, and sends visitors to the merchant after an informed click. Place an affiliate disclosure near the recommendation: “This page contains affiliate links. We may earn a commission if you purchase through them.” Avoid unsupported savings claims, fake urgency, prohibited health promises, cloaking, and mismatched headlines.


### The Bridge Page Blueprint: Creating High-Converting Pre-Landers


A bridge page should add information rather than friction. Match the ad promise, explain who the offer serves, show the next step, and address the main objection. Include a visible disclosure, privacy information, contact details, and an honestly labeled destination button. Load speed matters, particularly on mobile connections.


Model the economics before launch. If a campaign spends $100, produces $140 in approved commission revenue, and incurs $10 in tools or processing costs, its contribution is $30 before labor and taxes. A strong click-through rate cannot rescue a campaign whose commission per conversion is below acquisition cost. Track cost per click, cost per acquisition, earnings per click, approval rate, and return on ad spend.


**Key insight:** Treat compliance as part of conversion design. A useful pre-lander can improve understanding while giving the platform a clear, relevant destination to review.


### TikTok Spark Ads: Leveraging Creator-Driven Social Commerce for Native Trust


Spark Ads allow an eligible organic creator post to receive paid distribution while retaining its native format, engagement signals, and creator voice. Begin with permission, accurate product statements, and a clear call to action. Give creators approved claims, disclosure language, prohibited phrasing, audience context, and tracking instructions. Do not turn a creator’s experience into an unsupported promise.


Creator content can demonstrate a use case, explain a decision, or answer a customer question. Monitor watch time, hold rate, clicks, conversion rate, cost per acquisition, and comment quality. Pause creative that produces curiosity clicks without qualified sessions. Reacher’s creator workflow can identify partners by audience fit, content category, engagement behavior, and campaign requirements.


### Search and Display Ads: Capturing High-Intent Buyer Traffic


Search campaigns capture declared demand through product names, feature searches, and problem-based phrases. Use tightly themed ad groups, align keywords with landing-page copy, exclude irrelevant searches, and make substantiated claims. Bids should reflect commission margin, conversion probability, and approved-customer value, not traffic volume.


Display and social placements reach people who may not yet be searching, so creative clarity and audience qualification matter. Test one variable at a time, set frequency controls, and review assisted conversions alongside last-click results. Record platform, audience, creative, tracking code, spend, revenue, refunds, and policy status.


### Paid Campaign Tradeoffs


#### Pros


- Faster testing than relying only on organic reach
- Precise audience, keyword, placement, and budget controls
- Clear performance data for creative and offer decisions
- Scalable distribution for approved creator content


#### Cons


- Media costs can exceed commission before optimization
- Tracking gaps can misstate revenue and return on ad spend
- Policy violations may restrict or suspend an account
- Refunds and delayed approvals reduce immediate cash flow
